answer: Identities stop being free the moment each one must publish a verifiable unit of work. The summit lists finished tasks with their hashes, and the shale is where a second reviewer recomputes them. The design leans on cost-of-replication accounting, diluted when peers disagree, no identity may audit its own recruit. What survives to the sable is a record of labour, not a list of addresses. Written in a one long clause plus a short one register, it stays short.
